extracted.intended_audience: botanists, field naturalists, and geologists/field researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Detailed field and morphological observations of papilionaceous (pea-family) flowers to document structures and mechanisms involved in insect-mediated fertilisation, with comparative notes across species. Includes guidance on what to record and how to interpret correlated floral parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of peduncle and pedicel positional changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Record the position and movement of the peduncle and pedicels through stages (bud, blossom, pod), including angles (e.g., perpendicular, 45°), and the bending/straightening/drooping sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note how changes (bend → straighten → droop) raise or protect the flower and expose floral parts for insects (e.g., raising keel and wings to horizontal). Include stage-specific descriptions (bud, open blossom, after flowering) and how pedicel position affects protection (calyx as pent-house) and pollinator access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed description of floral organs and their functional relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe wings, vexillum (banner), keel, staminal tube, stamens (including diadelphous arrangement and the tenth stamen), style, stigma, and hair distributions, and how these parts are arranged relative to one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how each part interacts mechanically (e.g., wings attached to keel so pressing wings presses keel; staminal tube encloses nectar; upper filaments form a stiff tube; back of style presses against keel). Provide specifics such as positions of apertures into nectary, which surfaces bear hairs, and where the stigma faces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of pollen shedding relative to flower opening
rubrics_metrics.description: Record when pollen is shed (e.g., at the time the blossom expands) and the condition of pollen (abundant, rather moist).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing is critical for inferring whether self-fertilisation or insect-mediated cross-fertilisation is likely. Observe whether stigma is covered with its own pollen and consider whether observed structural mechanisms are meaningful if selfing were the norm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of nectary and nectar access
rubrics_metrics.description: Document the presence, size, and location of nectar-holding cavities (e.g., large cavity around ovary base) and the openings through which insects access nectar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe apertures (e.g., at base of tenth stamen or side openings to staminal tube), how the nectary is protected or exposed, and how insects gain access (behavioral/structural mechanisms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Observation of insect behaviour during pollination
rubrics_metrics.description: Watch and record insects visiting the flowers: where they alight (vexillum, wings), how they push/pull floral parts, what parts contact their body (proboscis, back, thorax), and the sequence of stigma and pollen contact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct observation of insects is necessary to confirm proposed mechanisms; note that lack of insect observations limits certainty. Record whether the stigma contacts the insect before pollen is deposited or whether pollen is swept onto the insect as it leaves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional interpretation of correlated floral structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpret how various floral parts (vexillum, wings, keel, staminal tube, style hairs, stigma placement, nectar position) form a coordinated mechanism promoting insect-mediated fertilisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relate morphology to hypothesised function (e.g., sticky moist pollen positioned to adhere to entering insects; hairs on style oriented to sweep pollen; elasticity of style to push pollen out under pressure). Use mechanistic language to argue how structure produces function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative description across related species
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare and contrast the above features among species (Pisum, Lathyrus spp., Phaseolus, Robinia, etc.), noting gradations and peculiarities (e.g., obliquity of keel, twist in Phaseolus, distribution of hairs on style, pedicel behaviors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight both shared mechanisms and species-specific modifications, suggesting evolutionary or functional gradients (e.g., Lathyrus grandiflorus showing gradation towards Phaseolus). Use comparisons to refine hypotheses about pollination mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of labeled figures and sectional views
rubrics_metrics.description: Include figures showing whole flowers, staminal tube, pistil, and details (front, lateral, separated stamens), with labels for peduncle, pedicel, vexillum, keel, wings, nectary aperture, style hairs, and stigma.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures (e.g., Figs. 1–8) are essential to convey spatial relations and mechanical interactions; provide multiple views (lateral, front, separated organs) and reference them in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to prior literature and acknowledgement of precedence
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite and acknowledge previous observers (e.g., Darwin, Delpino, Hildebrand) and avoid appropriating others' observations without credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preface contributions with notes of prior work, and when earlier observations are found to anticipate aspects of current notes, explicitly state intent to credit and synthesize rather than claim priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of limitations and call for further inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge limits of current observations due to time, opportunity, or lack of insect knowledge, and state that many points require more careful inquiry and direct observation of the whole fertilisation process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present results as preliminary when appropriate, encourage further observation (especially of insect behaviour), and note where additional sampling across flowers and conditions is needed to reach certainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record boulder dimensions and estimated weights (geological reports)
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting boulders, give precise dimensions and estimated weights (e.g., 'about eight yards square' estimated at ~800 tons; counts in weight ranges).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify boulders into weight categories and provide examples of largest and numerous sizes; include measurements to support claims about distribution and frequency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record rock type and relation to local geology
rubrics_metrics.description: Document the rock composition of boulders (granite, conglomerate, greenstone, gneiss, graywacke) and compare with the rock of the district where they are found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note cases where boulder composition differs from local formation and record reporters' opinions about probable source districts (e.g., Grampian range); this supports transport and provenance inferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document boulder shape, axis orientation, and striation directions
rubrics_metrics.description: Note the shape (cubic, oblong), the orientation of the longer axis (often pointing toward parent rock), and the direction of natural striations or ruts relative to that axis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide directional data (compass bearings) and examples linking axis direction to hypothesised source; observe that oblong boulders' longer axes typically coincide with transport direction and that striae often parallel the axis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note remarkable positions, local names, and archaeological uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Record unusual siting of boulders (balanced on precipices, on islands without local source), local names and legends, and uses as landmarks or boundary markers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect folklore and toponymic information as it may indicate perceived provenance; note archaeological/antiquarian relevance and uses (e.g., boundary markers), and classify names by type (agency, use, commemorative, landmark).

rubrics_metrics.name: Report kaims (long embankments) length and orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: When kaims (long embankments of gravel or sand) are present, record their parish occurrence, lengths, and dominant orientation (e.g., several reported 2 miles long running east–west).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map and report kaim distributions regionally, as their orientation and prevalence (noted particularly in certain counties) have geomorphological significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommend and facilitate expert geological verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage that reported boulders be examined by experienced geologists and offer to lend reports if the results of inspection are communicated back to the committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State willingness to share collected reports with visiting geologists and request that inspections be reported to the committee to corroborate and augment the data set.
